candidates.name: tx-hotel-heatmap
candidates.what_it_holds: TypeScript pipeline (scripts/build-data.ts) that parses Texas Comptroller hotel-occupancy-tax filings (data/hotels.csv: taxpayer, location, room count, reported revenue) at the INDIVIDUAL HOTEL level, plus data/periods/ holding per-period Comptroller files across multiple quarters, computing trailing-12-month RevPAR (revenue / rooms / 365) and ADR/occupancy per property; outputs a geocoded GeoJSON (public/hotels.geojson) bucketed by RevPAR percentile for a Next.js/Mapbox heatmap. Texas-only, county/city granularity via geocoding, updated 2026-07-22.
candidates.why_useful: Fills gap #8 (state-level hotel occupancy/lodging-tax data, individual-property RevPAR) with a real government administrative source (Texas Comptroller occupancy tax) at finer-than-market granularity, and demonstrates a repeatable pull/parse method that could be adapted to other states (Nevada, Florida bed tax) named explicitly in the same gap.
candidates.time_coverage: Multiple historical quarterly/monthly Comptroller filing periods through ~2026 (exact start year not stated in README excerpt)
candidates.size_hint: One CSV of TX hotel filings + a periods/ directory of historical per-period files; individual-hotel row grain, likely thousands of properties statewide
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Distinct from held Hawaii DBEDT / municipal STR registries and California TOT panel — this is Texas hotel (not STR) occupancy-tax data with property-level RevPAR, which we do not currently hold for Texas

candidates.name: Predicting_Hotel_Cancellation_Rate
candidates.what_it_holds: Notebook/pipeline predicting hotel demand and cancellation likelihood from 'reservations on-the-books' for a hotel chain; explicitly frames the on-the-books / pickup forecasting problem management-consulting style. Likely built on the same public Antonio/Almeida/Nunes Portugal hotel-booking dataset (H1/H2, ~2015-2017) already held, rather than new raw data.
candidates.why_useful: Illustrative of the on-the-books forecasting method / cancellation-rate framing relevant to the RNPL (reserve-now-pay-later) cancellation thesis (gap #3), though it appears to reuse a dataset we already hold rather than add new data.
candidates.geography: Unspecified hotel chain (likely Portugal, same as held Antonio dataset)
candidates.size_hint: Single notebook/script, no large committed dataset apparent
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Likely duplicate of already-held Portugal hotel-booking-demand dataset (Antonio/Almeida/Nunes); flagged only for the on-the-books/cancellation framing, not new data

notes: Both fallback search paths were degraded this run: WebSearch hit its shared 200/200 session budget almost immediately (before any of this scout's queries executed), duckduckgo.com/html and duckduckgo.com/lite both returned ECONNREFUSED on every attempt (network egress to that host appears blocked from this environment), and www.bing.com/search via WebFetch turned out to be non-functional as a search proxy -- a sanity check with a nonsense query ('test query xyz123') returned the same kind of generic, non-query-matching result set (speed-test sites, dictionary entries) as the real queries did, and a query for 'hotel'-related terms always surfaced the same OTA marketing pages (Booking.com, Expedia, Kayak, Trivago) regardless of the site: operator or exact phrase used -- so Bing results in this session should be treated as unusable, not as evidence of absence. The only working channel was `gh search repos` against the GitHub API, which is rate-limited at 5,000/hr SHARED across all ~200+ scouts running concurrently in this sweep; I got through roughly a dozen queries before being cut off entirely (403 rate-limit on every subsequent call, confirmed via `gh api rate_limit`). Within that budget, GitHub's own repo search returned almost nothing for the specific theme (hotel booking-pace/pickup curves, OTA Insight/Lighthouse/Key Data/Transparent samples, revenue-management forward curves) beyond a large volume of near-identical student Power BI/Tableau portfolio dashboards (the 'AtliQ Hotels' mock dataset, or re-slices of the Kaggle Antonio/Almeida/Nunes Portugal hotel-booking-demand file already held) that add no new data and were excluded per the task rules. No OTA Insight/Lighthouse/Transparent/Key Data sample export, no AirDNA sample, no NCLH advance-ticket-sales dataset, and no dedicated cancellation-lead-time distribution dataset surfaced in the queries that did run. The one genuinely new find (tx-hotel-heatmap) came from a generic 'revpar hotel' query, not a pace/pickup-specific one -- suggesting the theme's actual GitHub footprint (real booking-curve/pace data, as opposed to commercial-vendor names) may simply be very thin, consistent with how proprietary that data category is (OTA Insight/Lighthouse, Key Data, Transparent, AirDNA are all paid SaaS with no public sample exports we could locate). Recommend a follow-up scout retry this exact theme once the shared GitHub API rate limit resets and/or WebSearch budget resets, using `gh search repos` queries for: 'hotel occupancy tax' + state names (Nevada, Florida, Hawaii bed tax) to extend the tx-hotel-heatmap pattern to other US states named in gap #8; 'NCLH advance ticket sales' / '10-Q parser' for the cruise book-ahead analogue (gap #18); and 'Expedia ICDM' / 'Kaggle hotel search log' for older click/booking-curve competition data mirrors.
